tasks.commitBody:
The roster row labeled a bare JWT an invite link. Two surfaces share one mint; only the admin surface composed a URL — the roster row borrowed its strings ('Invite link', the bearer warning) but not its value construction, so it rendered the label, a colon, and a raw token that a recipient can do nothing with. Two live bearer tokens reached chat in one day as screenshots of exactly that label, which is also why display-to-transcribe had to become click-to-copy.

The row's value now goes through the same buildInviteUrl the admin surface uses — the single shared helper, which throws rather than fabricate a relative or dead link — and both producers behind the row, invite and resend, converge on the one assignment site that now composes. The value renders as a readonly input: clicking it selects the text and copies through the copy implementation extracted from #345 into a shared module — one function, one set of failure semantics, now with exactly one clipboard call site in the tree — with the confirmation in a per-row persistent status region and failure in a per-row alert, reusing the existing keys in all four locales. The admin surface was refactored onto the same module with its entire #345 test suite passing unmodified, which is the proof the extraction changed nothing. The new per-row copy state resets where the invite map already resets — on collective switch and on deselection — so nothing leaks across identities. The bearer warning stays, untouched: it is the only thing on the row telling an admin what they are holding.

Closes #346

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)
